title: Decision-weighted Model Taxonomy & Procurement Scorecard Toolkit
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build a decision-weighted taxonomy and accompanying scorecard tool that converts continuous model-landscape signals into procurement-ready priorities. This ticket scopes the PM deliverable and the minimal data pipeline and UX to enable procurement and platform teams to make defensible provisioning and contract decisions when models appear/disappear or change pricing/latency profiles.
background: We currently track dozens of open models and vendor endpoints but lack a reproducible, auditable way to translate supply signals (availability, latency SLA, quantization support, licensing) into a procurement priority. Procurement and platform teams keep ad-hoc spreadsheets that cause delays and missed opportunities. This initiative aims to reduce time-to-decision and surface trade-offs (cost vs latency vs compliance risk) with an explorable scorecard.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible taxonomy that maps model attributes to decision dimensions (availability, latency impact, quantization compatibility, legal/licensing risk, switching cost)
A scorecard calculation (explainable weights) exported as CSV and available via a simple UI mock that ranks models for procurement by priority and expected impact
Integration pipeline that ingests model catalog signals (availability, region coverage, cost/ token) on a nightly cadence
Procurement and Platform partners validate 3 representative scenarios and accept the score outputs as decision-support (sign-off recorded in comments)
Basic audit trail: for any score, record the input snapshot timestamp and the weight configuration identifier
tasks: Define signal ingestion schema with Data Eng (fields, refresh cadence)
Prototype score calculation in notebook and publish CSV outputs
Design low-fidelity UI mock for procurement console (Designer review)
Run 3 scenario validations with procurement and platform teams
Add lightweight audit metadata to model catalog export
risks: Signal quality: availability and latency data may be noisy across regions
Buy-in risk: procurement may prefer incumbent scoring heuristics unless scorecard is auditable
Maintenance cost: weight tuning could drift without a lightweight governance process
